report.summary: Chunk 3 of gated_writes.py defines _provider_receipt, _spec_for, and _curated_relay_gate with extensive docstring claims. Most claims about external code are uncheckable; internal logic is consistent.
risks: _provider_receipt | low | Returns empty dict via `or None` logic; if detail has keys but no Mapping subfields, receipt is empty -> None. Possibly unexpected if caller expects dict. | Verify caller handles None correctly.

handoff.purpose: Define helper functions for provider receipt projection, task spec construction, and composed relay+curated gate.

symbols.name: _provider_receipt
symbols.note: Projects a small operational dict from an offload runner result, extracting routing/action facts, measured writes, and rewrite activation/skip provenance.

symbols.name: _spec_for
symbols.note: Constructs a TaskSpec for an assignment, incorporating gate, model, and metadata.

symbols.name: _curated_relay_gate
symbols.note: Composes _relay_gate and command_gate in order, returning both verdicts unchanged.

claims.text: The full provider result lives on ``AttemptResult.runner_detail``.
claims.why: AttemptResult.runner_detail is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: The write-wave projection used to drop it, collapsing every provider refusal into ``the runner produced no change to gate``.
claims.why: No evidence of prior projection or 'runner produced no change to gate' string in this chunk.

claims.text: Keep only routing/action facts, measured writes, and rewrite activation/skip provenance -- never prompts, repository content, or arbitrary model prose.
claims.why: Function extracts keys: provider, model, action, wrote, did_work from detail; and handoff keys: windowed_rewrite, skipped, slice_context_dropped. No prompts or repo content.

claims.text: ``gate`` is the task's OWN curated command gate ({"argv", "cwd", "timeout_s"}), forwarded by the caller from the picker candidate that produced this work.

``None``/empty reproduces the previous behaviour byte-for-byte, including the effect-key digest: ``TaskSpec.body()`` admits ``gate`` into the canonical body only when ``gate_argv`` is non-empty, so no task that lacks one sees its digest move.
claims.why: TaskSpec.body() not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: WHY THIS IS NOT A NEW EXECUTION RISK. The argv is repo-authored, not model-authored: ``spine/picker.py`` builds it (docref's is ``sys.executable -m daedalus.spine.docref_gate ...``), and the work-queue source validates it as a NUL-free string array out of a repo-curated file.
claims.why: spine/picker.py not present; validation logic not shown.

claims.text: It is then executed by ``spine.attempt.command_gate`` as an argv list with no shell, at LOW INTEGRITY inside containment, in a Job Object, in the candidate's own worktree -- the same instrument, with the same containment, that already runs every default pytest gate.
claims.why: spine.attempt.command_gate not defined; containment details not shown.

claims.text: A model-written patch cannot reach this path without a human `git merge` first, because the picker reads the primary checkout and promotion stops at an integration branch.
claims.why: Picker and promotion logic not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``_relay_gate`` AND the task's own curated command gate, in that order.
claims.why: Code calls relay = _relay_gate(box) first, then defines _gate that calls relay(ctx) and then command_gate(ctx) in that order.

claims.text: THIS COMPOSITION IS THE WHOLE POINT, and it exists because putting ``gate_argv`` on the TaskSpec alone would have done NOTHING: ``TaskAttempt.__init__`` gives an explicitly-passed ``gate=`` precedence over ``task.gate_argv``, and this module always passes one.
claims.why: TaskAttempt.__init__ not defined; evidence of module always passing gate not shown.

claims.text: 1. ``_relay_gate`` first, as a PRECONDITION. It is the only check that catches ``offload()`` finishing ``escalated_after_verify_fail`` with a NON-EMPTY ``wrote`` -- a write it could not fully roll back, kept visible on purpose. Those bytes are a failed run's debris; judging them with a docref re-scan could well return "references resolve" and would promote debris. Replacing the relay gate rather than preceding it would have opened exactly that hole.
claims.why: offload() and its behavior not in this chunk; _relay_gate implementation not shown.

claims.text: 2. The curated command gate second, as the DISCRIMINATOR -- the thing that actually knows whether THIS task succeeded.
claims.why: Code calls command_gate(ctx) after relay(ctx) and uses its result.

claims.text: Both verdicts are returned UNCHANGED (never re-wrapped into a fresh GateResult), so containment attestations and gate output survive whichever one decides. Fail-closed: both must pass.
claims.why: Return value logic not fully shown; GateResult not defined in this chunk.

observations.what: _provider_receipt returns None if detail is not a Mapping or if receipt is empty (e.g., detail has keys but none of the extracted ones). This could surprise callers expecting a dict.
_spec_for constructs metadata dict with optional keys; rewrite_windows and model are added conditionally. The gate_timeout_s defaults to _DEFAULT_GATE_TIMEOUT_S if not provided.

_curated_relay_gate defines an inner _gate function that calls relay and command_gate; the outer function returns the inner function (closure). The docstring claims order matters but the code does not show how the inner function is used.
